title: Roof and fragile-surface work
audience: Workers and supervisors who go onto roofs, skylights, sheeting or any surface that may not carry a person.
learningOutcomes: Identify the fall and falling-object risks of roof work, including the roof edge, openings and fragile material.
Recognise fragile and brittle roofing, and the controls that apply before a person walks on it.
Describe the access, edge and anchor requirements a roof job needs.
State the stop-work decision for a roof that is unsafe or unknown.

instruction.heading: Why roofs need their own rules
instruction.body: A roof combines several hazards. A person can fall off the edge, fall through a surface that cannot bear weight, slip down a pitched surface, be struck by falling objects, and be affected by the weather. One source describes falls off the edge, falls through fragile roof sheets and skylights, and slips from the eaves on pitched roofs. Another adds that age, sun, pollution, chemicals, storms and overloading all make a roof less reliable over time. Treat each roof as unknown until its condition has been checked.

instruction.heading: Fragile and brittle surfaces
instruction.body: A brittle roof is one that will not carry a person at every point on its surface, because of its material, age or weathering. The sources name plastic, glass, mineral fibre and thin corrugated sheeting as typical examples. Skylights, old fibre-cement and worn tiles can also fail. Before anyone walks on a roof, find out what it is made of, look for signs of failure such as crazing, discolouration, rust through, soft spots and cracked sheets, and then decide the controls. Do not test a sheet by stepping on it. The worker's judgement is not a control. The fragile areas must be marked, covered or avoided, and crawling boards or a platform used wherever the roof has to be crossed.

instruction.heading: Edges and openings
instruction.body: The edge is usually the main fall risk. Where an edge is unprotected, use a guardrail, a parapet at a safe height, a scaffold or work platform, a warning line with a restraint or arrest measure behind it, or a safety net. Where a warning line is used, anyone working between the line and the edge needs a harness and fall arrest. Cover or guard every skylight, roof light and opening before work near it starts.

instruction.heading: Access to the roof
instruction.body: The sources recommend a stable, independent scaffold or tower for access to a roof, even for short work. It must be tied in or supported so it cannot rock or tip. Plan the rescue route before access is set up. A ladder is for access to the start of the roof only and must extend above the edge. The ladder rules are in “Choosing and using ladders for trade and exterior work”, and the scaffold and tower checks are in “Scaffold and mobile tower checks before use”.

instruction.heading: Falling material and tools
instruction.body: Keep materials and tools clear of the edge, secure them against wind, and never throw them up or down. Catch netting or boards stop small items from falling. Keep people from walking under roof work. One source asks that stacking and storage on roofs be kept to a minimum and secured against wind, and that waste be taken off by a chute or container rather than thrown.

instruction.heading: Weather on the roof
instruction.body: Wet, icy, windy or hot weather changes the risk. One source says that wet, windy or icy conditions can make footing and control much harder, so controls must be applied. Stop roof work in gusty wind, rain or ice, and reassess after any change.

instruction.heading: Overhead services and solar
instruction.body: Overhead lines, inverters and the cabling of solar arrays add risk on a roof. Check for them before the work starts. The solar and electrical rules are in the solar course and in “Electrical, solar and overhead services”, and this lesson does not authorise any work near electrical systems.

procedure: Find out the roof material, its age and any known weak areas, and mark the fragile zones.
Confirm the edge protection or the fall-arrest plan before anyone steps onto the roof.
Set up the access scaffold or tower and check it.
Cover or guard each skylight and opening.
Set materials and tools clear of the edge, and secure them.
Use crawling boards or a platform for every crossing of a fragile area.
Check the weather again at each change, and stop if it turns.
Leave the roof clear, and record the roof condition and any defect found.

workedExamples.situation: A worker must check a corrugated-sheet roof where a translucent plastic section sits beside a skylight.
workedExamples.reasoning: Identify the translucent sheets as fragile, mark them, and cover or guard the area before anyone walks on the roof. Use crawling boards or a platform, and do not walk on the sheets.

workedExamples.situation: A roofer is asked to clean a pitched tile roof with no guardrail, and the eave is about four metres above a path.
workedExamples.reasoning: Unprotected edges on a pitched roof need edge protection, a platform, or a safety net, with fall arrest only where the others are not possible. The job cannot start on a plan that relies on a harness alone, and a rescue plan has to be ready.

equipmentAndPpe: Crawling boards or a roof ladder
Safety netting where it is specified
Harness and lanyard (see “Fall protection and arrest systems” and “Inspecting and fitting harnesses and lanyards”)

commonErrors.error: Assuming a roof is sound because it looks intact.
commonErrors.prevention: Identify the material and check for signs of failure before any step is taken.

commonErrors.error: Walking on the sheets between the supports.
commonErrors.prevention: Use crawling boards or a platform, and keep to the supports.

commonErrors.error: Leaving skylights uncovered while work continues near them.
commonErrors.prevention: Cover or guard each opening before work near it starts.

commonErrors.error: Dropping a bucket or tool from the roof.
commonErrors.prevention: Use a container and a hauling line, and clear the area below.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Warning: fragile or brittle roofing will not carry a person at every point. Treat an unknown roof as fragile until it has been checked.
Warning: never work at an unprotected roof edge without the edge controls named in the plan.
The roof edge heights in the sources, the warning-line distance and the lightning distances come from non-Australian sources, so check with the relevant regulator before relying on this point.
The Safe Work Australia falls code is the national reference for falls at workplaces.
NSW: a new code for work on roofs of commercial and industrial buildings took effect in May 2026. The part read excludes residential roofs and did not address soft washing or gutter cleaning.

Licence notice: this lesson does not grant a licence or authority to work on roofs, to apply chemicals at height or to work near electrical systems. Check with the relevant regulator whether a licence is needed for chemical soft washing at height before relying on this point.

qualityStandard: The roof material and condition are recorded before access.
Fragile zones are marked and controlled before work starts.
The edge control is named and checked before work near the edge.
documentationEvidence: Roof condition note with fragile areas marked
summary: Treat an unknown roof as fragile until it has been checked.
An unprotected edge needs a physical control before a harness is considered.
Cover every opening, and keep materials clear of the edge.
Stop roof work in weather that makes footing or the surface unsafe.

knowledgeChecks.question: A roof sheet looks intact but shows crazing and soft spots. What is the right treatment?
options: Treat it as fragile, and avoid walking on it until controls have been set up.
Walk across it quickly, keeping weight near the sheet's edges.
Stand only on the ridge and walk along it slowly to the far end of the roof
Assume it is safe because it was intact last year and it has been walked on since

knowledgeChecks.question: Which action is safe where a roof edge is unprotected?
options: Work at the edge without a harness, because the edge is close and the crew can shout to each other
Put an edge control in place, such as a guardrail, parapet, platform or safety net, before work near the edge.
Rely on a sign at the bottom of the ladder and a rope tied to the gutter and the chimney near the edge
Stand clear of the edge only when it rains and keep working when it is dry and warm outside

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should materials stay back from a roof edge?
options: To keep the edge clear for photographs and to show the client the work
To stop them falling onto people below, and to keep the working surface clear.
To increase the roof's load limit and to keep the sheets flat on the roof
Because materials are placed on the roof edge to hold the sheet down.

officialReferences.title: Model Code of Practice: Managing the risk of falls at workplaces (Safe Work Australia)
officialReferences.pageDate: No date shown (publication date field blank; the page says the model WHS laws were created in 2011)
officialReferences.covers: The model Code of Practice says to check with the regulator whether it has legal effect in the jurisdiction. It gives no hierarchy of control and no numeric height trigger; its scope refers to falls from one level to another that are reasonably likely to cause injury. It does not mention roof edge heights, warning-line distances or lightning distances.

officialReferences.title: Working at heights (Safe Work Australia)
officialReferences.covers: Read 2026-11-03: construction work with a risk of falling more than 2 metres is high risk construction work for which a Safe Work Method Statement must be prepared. The control order is work on the ground or a solid construction first, then fall prevention devices, then work positioning systems, with fall arrest as the last option. The page does not address roof-specific rules or the NSW roof code.
